extracted.intended_audience: market participants, exchanges (SROs), trading permit holders, data vendors, and members of the public who may submit comments on SEC rule filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for submitting comments on proposed SRO rule changes and the substantive standards the SEC and exchanges must state and meet when filing proposed rule changes (including market-data and fee proposals). Includes filing procedures, publication rules, legal standards (Section 6(b), Rule 19b-4(f)(6), Regulation NMS), and example product/fee-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for submitting comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may be submitted electronically using the Commission’s internet comment form (https://www.sec.gov/rules/sro.shtml) or by email to rule-comments@sec.gov, or as paper comments sent in triplicate to the Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the file number on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review comments more efficiently, please use only one method of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference file number and deadline requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions should refer to the applicable file number (e.g., SR-NYSETEX-2025-10 or SR-CBOE-2025-035) and should be submitted on or before the stated deadline (e.g., June 12, 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The file number should be included on the subject line of email submissions and on paper filings; follow the specific deadline stated in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and FOIA exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will post all comments on its internet website (https://www.sec.gov/rules/sro.shtml). Copies of submissions, amendments, written statements, and communications between the Commission and any person (other than those exempt under 5 U.S.C. 552) will be available for website viewing and printing in the Commission’s Public Reference Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; submit only information you wish to make publicly available. The Commission may redact in part or withhold from publication material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. Viewing hours and location are specified (Public Reference Room, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC, 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. on official business days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation content expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views, and arguments concerning whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address legal consistency and policy implications (e.g., whether the proposal is consistent with Section 6(b), Regulation NMS) and may include factual data and arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 19b-4(f)(6) / Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) effectiveness criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed rule change filed under Section 19(b)(3)(A) and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) normally becomes effective upon filing if it (i) does not significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) does not impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) does not become operative prior to 30 days from the date of filing (unless a shorter time is designated by the Commission consistent with investor protection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 19b-4(f)(6) also requires an SRO to give the Commission written notice of its intent to file the proposed rule change, along with a brief description and text, at least five business days prior to filing (or such shorter time as designated). The Commission may waive the 30-day operative delay if consistent with protection of investors and the public interest, and may summarily suspend the rule change within 60 days if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission waiver considerations for operative delay
rubrics_metrics.description: In deciding whether to waive the 30-day operative delay the Commission considers the proposed rule’s impact on efficiency, competition, and capital formation (see 15 U.S.C. 78c(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A filing may request waiver; the Commission will evaluate whether the proposal presents novel issues and whether immediate availability benefits investors or otherwise is consistent with protection of investors and the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 6(b)(5) substantive standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed exchange rules must be consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act: designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, promote just and equitable principles of trade, foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in facilitating transactions in securities, remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, protect investors and the public interest, and not be designed to permit unfair discrimination among customers, brokers, or dealers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchange filings should explain how the proposal furthers these objectives (e.g., by increasing transparency, competition, or investor protections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 11A / Regulation NMS consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should be consistent with Section 11A of the Act insofar as they support fair competition among brokers/dealers and availability of information with respect to quotations and transactions; they should also be consistent with Rule 603 of Regulation NMS, which requires that distribution of quotation/transaction information be on terms that are not unreasonably discriminatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a product is proprietary and voluntary, exchanges should explain voluntary subscription terms, alternative sources of data, and nondiscriminatory access/terms (e.g., offering via multiple networks like LCN and IGN).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden on competition disclosure (Section 6(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: An exchange must state whether the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the Act (Section 6(b)(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the competitive landscape (e.g., presence of substitute products from other exchanges), why the proposal enhances or does not unreasonably burden competition, and how market forces constrain pricing/availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide statement of purpose, basis, and comment discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization must include statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discuss any comments it received on the proposed rule change (these are presented in Items I, II, and III of the filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text of those statements must be available for examination at the places specified (exchange website, principal office, Commission’s Public Reference Room).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of proposed rule text and exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of the proposed rule change (and exhibits such as fee schedule text) must be provided and made publicly available on the exchange’s website, at the exchange’s Office of the Secretary, and at the Commission’s Public Reference Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filings typically identify exhibits (e.g., Exhibit 5) containing the proposed rule/fee text; include links or references where the public can access the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations to prior related releases and comparative products
rubrics_metrics.description: Filings commonly cite prior Securities Act or Exchange Act release numbers and point to analogous products offered by other exchanges as part of the justification and competitive analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific prior release citations and examples of similar products (e.g., NYSE Order Imbalances, Nasdaq NOII, Open-Close Data from other options exchanges) to demonstrate precedent and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for proprietary market-data product proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposing a proprietary market-data product, an exchange should explain the product’s content (e.g., Auction Imbalance Information: Total Imbalance, Market Imbalance, Indicative Match Price, Matched Volume), dissemination timing, intended distribution networks, and how providing the product promotes transparency and investor access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain availability (symbols covered), distribution channels (e.g., LCN, IGN), whether product will be charged for and plans to file fees if adopted, and how the product fits within Regulation NMS objectives (competition, efficiency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee-change and discount program standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee proposals (including temporary discounts) should be reasonable, equitable, not unfairly discriminatory, and consistent with the Act and Regulation NMS; they should promote competition and explain how the fee change furthers investor and market interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the rationale (e.g., encourage use of data, allow testing at discounted rates), competitive context (number of exchanges, market share), and confirm that purchases are voluntary and available equally to eligible purchasers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific operational conditions for temporary discounts
rubrics_metrics.description: As exemplified by the Cboe filing: a temporary 20% discount applies to ad-hoc purchases of historical Open-Close Data where a single order totals $20,000 or more; the discount is applied on an order-by-order basis and the Exchange will not aggregate purchases across a billing cycle for qualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The discount cannot be combined with other discounts (including academic discounts); an example is provided where a $25,000 order would be discounted to $20,000 (20% discount = $5,000). Program effective dates must be specified (e.g., April 23, 2025 through June 30, 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-product descriptive standards (EOD vs Intraday)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and operational characteristics of data products should be clear: End-of-Day (EOD) Open-Close Data is an end-of-day volume summary by option series and origin; Intraday Open-Close Data is updated every 10 minutes (snapshots captured and provided within five minutes of each 10-minute period). Both are proprietary to the exchange and do not include other exchanges' data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details on data granularity (by origin, side, price, transaction type), trade-size buckets, update timing (example: first intraday calculation by ~9:42 a.m. ET for 9:30–9:40 snapshot), and distribution mechanism (subscription or ad-hoc purchase).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compulsory / voluntary nature of proprietary data products
rubrics_metrics.description: Proprietary data products offered by exchanges are voluntary; neither the exchange nor data vendors are required by rule to make such data available, and purchasers may elect alternatives (real-time consolidated, free delayed consolidated, or other proprietary feeds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchange should note voluntarily available alternatives and explain that vendors/subscribers can discontinue use at any time; this fact is used to support nondiscriminatory access and competitive framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission summary-suspension authority and follow-up proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time within 60 days of filing, the Commission may summarily temporarily suspend a proposed rule change if it appears necessary or appropriate in the public interest or for investor protection, and if suspended, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine approval or disapproval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This authority is discretionary and is part of the Commission’s review process for filings effective upon filing under Rule 19b-4(f)(6).
